target.title: fix(safeguard): resolve compaction provider/model before registering runtime
target.body:
Fixes #57901.

## What Problem This Solves

Safeguard auto-compaction registered and preferred the active session model even when `agents.defaults.compaction.model` selected a different summarization model. That made the documented override ineffective in normal embedded runs; an unresolved override could also degrade to `model: undefined` without explaining which configured target failed.

## Summary

Safeguard auto-compaction now honors `agents.defaults.compaction.model` when embedded extensions register their runtime state.

- Reuse `resolveEmbeddedCompactionTarget` before safeguard registration.
- Resolve the selected provider/model through the active `ModelRegistry`, including alias/configured-model support.
- Forward auth-profile, harness-runtime, and `modelSelectionLocked` inputs from both normal runs and explicit compaction runs.
- Prefer the registered compaction model over `ctx.model` inside the safeguard hook.
- Preserve locked native-harness sessions on their pinned model.
- When a configured override cannot be resolved, emit a warning and retain the active session model instead of silently registering `model: undefined`.
- Use the resolved compaction model's context window.
- Remove the PR-only proof script and unrelated collateral churn; the PR now changes six focused source/test files.

## Behavior

For a normal embedded run, the configured compaction target is resolved through the same shared resolver used by explicit compaction. A provider switch drops the session's provider-specific auth profile. If selection is locked to a native harness, the configured override is intentionally ignored.

For the explicit `/compact` path, the caller has already resolved and loaded the compaction target. Registration detects that the target matches and keeps that loaded model.

The safeguard hook now uses:

```ts
const model = runtime?.model ?? ctx.model;
```

That lets a configured compaction model win while preserving the session model as the no-override or unresolved-override fallback.

## Evidence

Validated on the synchronized merge tree:

- PR head: `74e144c000adcb765e05531c146f6210426eb281`
- Main cutoff / second parent: `262baedcf7fa3d66dc35cce7d0253e0a31f0cc0e`
- Final diff: 6 files, +277/-17

Checks:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed
- Core test TypeScript project (`test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json`) — passed
- Focused Vitest suites — 4 files, 154 tests passed:
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.extensions.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compaction-runtime-context.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/extensions.test.ts`

- `oxfmt --check` on all six changed files — passed

The affected `src/agents` full-core lint shard also passed. The full repository-wide lint command was not completed end-to-end locally after upstream moved during validation; CI remains the authoritative full gate.

## Testing scope

No live provider API call was made. Regression coverage exercises target resolution, provider-switch auth handling, native-harness model locking, runtime registration, unresolved-model warning/fallback, and the safeguard summarizer receiving the runtime-selected model.

target.title: Fix stack-safe large attachment handling
target.body:
## Summary

Closes #90098.

This branch is now rebased onto current OpenClaw architecture and deliberately narrowed to the parts still missing from `main`:

- replace the gateway's full-payload data-URL capture regex with bounded index/slice parsing;
- replace the Control UI send-path data-URL capture regex in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.ts`;
- replace the pasted-image full-payload regex in `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-composer.ts` with a bounded header check plus iterative payload validation;
- discard stale failed composer queue entries created by the old `Maximum call stack size exceeded` failure;
- add focused gateway and current-UI regression coverage.

Current `main` already contains iterative base64 validation and the broader 20 MB / 20-page inbound extraction policy, so this update keeps those upstream implementations and drops the obsolete extraction-limit/config churn from the older branch.

## What problem this solves

Multi-megabyte PDF/image data URLs were still passed through regexes that captured the entire base64 payload. On sufficiently large browser or gateway sends, V8 could throw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` before the attachment reached normal validation/offload handling. Failed Control UI sends carrying that historical error could also be restored and replayed after upgrade.

The new parsing keeps regex use bounded to a short MIME header and processes the payload by index/iteration.

## Current changed paths

- `src/gateway/chat-attachments.ts`
- `src/gateway/chat-attachments.test.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-composer.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/composer-persistence.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/composer-persistence.test.ts`

## Verification

Regression coverage on the current file layout now includes:

- a 12 MiB gateway data URL parsed/offloaded without a full-payload regex;
- a large Control UI attachment serialized through `chat.send`;
- a large pasted image converted through the current composer;
- rejection of invalid pasted base64;
- identifiable pre-fix attachment stack-overflow records dropped during restore, while current failures and unrelated text failures with the same generic V8 phrase remain durable and retryable via a stored item-format marker.

Fresh GitHub CI is running on exact head `73169d41851fa41bbe502df3cab0e04d3f448a7c`, which contains the shared upstream cutoff `262baedcf7fa3d66dc35cce7d0253e0a31f0cc0e` and the narrowed legacy-cleanup repair.

Additional exact-head repair validation: 281 focused Control UI tests pass across composer persistence, chat state, and chat send; formatting, targeted oxlint, and diff checks also pass. The storage-only marker is retained across internal normalization only for affected failed attachment records and is stripped from public queue snapshots.

## Real behavior evidence

The original branch was validated with a real Chrome upload of a 9.18 MB, 8-page PDF (roughly a 12 MB base64 data URL) against a live gateway. The upload completed without `RangeError`, was offloaded, and the model received extracted page content. That live run was on the pre-port head; this update ports the same stack-safe parsing behavior to today's gateway and UI paths and adds exact-path regression tests. No new live Signal/provider/device claim is being made for this merge-only port.

Generated with AI assistance; all security-sensitive parsing remains fail-closed for malformed payloads.

target.title: fix(acp): ACP session startup fails when backend does not advertise thinking config
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103802 — ACP sessions can fail at startup with:

```
AcpRuntimeError: ACP backend "acpx" does not accept config key "thinking".: code=ACP_BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED_CONTROL
```

This happens when thinking is inherited from defaults/model profile and then applied to a backend that does not advertise a thinking config option.

## Why This Change Was Made

This patch preserves explicit user intent while tolerating inherited defaults only when unsupported:

1. **Track thinking provenance at spawn/init time**
   - `thinkingSource: "explicit" | "default"` is recorded when ACP runtime options are created
   - persisted in ACP session metadata as `runtimeOptionSources.thinking`

2. **Apply strictness by provenance in runtime controls**
   - if backend advertises keys and a thinking key is not supported:
     - `thinkingSource === "default"` → skip (best-effort inherited default)
     - `thinkingSource === "explicit"` (or unknown) → throw `ACP_BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED_CONTROL` (fail-visible explicit intent)

3. **Sync provenance on mutation paths**
   - `setSessionConfigOption` with a thinking key → sets provenance to "explicit"
   - `updateSessionRuntimeOptions` with thinking in patch → sets provenance to "explicit"
   - `resetSessionRuntimeOptions` → clears provenance

4. **Preserve existing configured/model-profile defaults on capable backends**
   - defaults are still inherited and applied where supported

## User Impact

- ACP sessions against limited backends no longer fail due to inherited default thinking values.
- Explicit `sessions_spawn(thinking: ...)` remains strict and fails visibly when unsupported.
- Changing thinking after spawn (via setConfigOption or updateRuntimeOptions) correctly updates provenance.
- Configured/model-profile thinking defaults still apply on backends that support them.

## Changes Since Last Review

### Rebased onto latest upstream/main
Branch was 50 commits behind and conflicted. Rebased cleanly — all 5 commits applied without semantic conflict.

### Legacy migration added
Added `backfillAcpSessionProvenance()` in `ensureAdditiveStateColumns` — when the new `runtime_option_sources_json` column is added, existing rows with `runtime_options_json` containing `"thinking"` are backfilled with `{"thinking":"default"}`. This ensures pre-patch sessions with inherited thinking are tolerated after upgrade instead of continuing to fail.

### Migration proof
```
=== BEFORE MIGRATION ===
[
  { "session_key": "agent:opencode:acp:s1", "runtime_options_json": "{\"thinking\":\"high\",\"model\":\"gpt-4\"}" },
  { "session_key": "agent:codex:acp:s2", "runtime_options_json": "{\"model\":\"claude-3\"}" },
  { "session_key": "agent:opencode:acp:s3", "runtime_options_json": "{\"thinking\":\"high\",\"model\":\"gpt-4\"}" }
]

=== AFTER MIGRATION (backfilled 2 rows) ===
[
  { "session_key": "agent:opencode:acp:s1", "runtime_options_json": "...", "runtime_option_sources_json": "{\"thinking\":\"default\"}" },
  { "session_key": "agent:codex:acp:s2", "runtime_options_json": "...", "runtime_option_sources_json": null },
  { "session_key": "agent:opencode:acp:s3", "runtime_options_json": "...", "runtime_option_sources_json": "{\"thinking\":\"default\"}" }
]
```
Rows with thinking get backfilled as "default". Rows without thinking stay NULL (correct — no provenance needed).

## Evidence

- 20 files changed, ~320 insertions, ~5 deletions
- Rebased onto latest `upstream/main` (commit `8310c565`)
- All tests pass:

```
$ pnpm vitest run src/acp/control-plane/manager.runtime-config.test.ts
✓ 23 passed (including 4 new provenance tests)

$ pnpm vitest run src/acp/runtime/session-meta.test.ts
✓ 9 passed

$ pnpm vitest run src/agents/acp-spawn.test.ts
✓ 66 passed

$ pnpm vitest run src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts
✓ 23 passed
```

- Legacy migration verified: pre-patch rows with `runtime_options_json` containing `"thinking"` are backfilled with `{"thinking":"default"}` on column addition
- Rows without thinking remain NULL (no provenance needed)

target.title: fix(gateway): keep worker SSH tunnel stderr tails UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Worker SSH tunnel failures retain bounded stdout/stderr diagnostics before `processError()` exposes them to operators. Raw `.slice(-4096)` could begin the retained text on the low half of an emoji or another non-BMP character, producing malformed UTF-16 in the failure message.

This is the production `createWorkerSshRunner()` path used by the worker tunnel manager when SSH exits before its ready marker.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both output streams now share one small `appendBoundedDiagnosticTail` path backed by the repository's canonical `sliceUtf16Safe` helper. The 4096-code-unit cap, redaction, ready-marker behavior, reconnect policy, and success path are unchanged.

The regression invokes the real child-process runner and crosses the exact retention boundary. The maintainer refactor reduced the patch from 53 added lines to 23 while keeping the production boundary under test.

## User Impact

**Before:** A worker SSH failure could show a corrupted leading character when oversized remote output placed a surrogate pair across the retained-tail boundary.

**After:** The incomplete surrogate is discarded and the operator-facing diagnostic remains well-formed.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/gateway/worker-environments/tunnel.ts`
- Regression: `src/gateway/worker-environments/tunnel.test.ts`
- Exact tested head: `f3bfd319b7c1a741976d1cf5f2a24c48858e59f0`
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox: `run_ff21a762ee41`, public network, no Tailscale, no instance profile, no credential hydration
- Command: `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/tunnel.test.ts`
- Result: exit 0
- Fresh autoreview: no findings, correctness confidence 0.94
- Hosted exact-head CI: running

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** worker SSH failure details no longer split UTF-16 surrogate pairs at the bounded stdout/stderr tail.
- **Reachability:** `createWorkerTunnelManager` -> `createWorkerSshRunner().start(...)` -> child output handlers -> `appendBoundedDiagnosticTail` -> `processError(stderr)` -> rejected `ready` promise.
- **Boundary crossed:** real spawned child stderr into the operator-facing production error.
- **Fix classification:** root-cause fix.
- **Proof gap:** no live remote SSH worker was needed; forwarding and connection behavior are unchanged.

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
Current head: `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`.

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false vitest run --project extension-codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` passed (149 tests)

- `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` passed (10 tests)
- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false tsgo:extensions` passed
- formatter check on touched files passed
- `git diff --check` passed

## Public SDK Contract
This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`
- generic tool progress kind: `TOOL_PROGRESS_KIND = "tool-progress"`
- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`
- existing fast-mode kind remains: `FAST_MODE_AUTO_PROGRESS_KIND = "fast-mode-auto"`

Codex no longer exports Codex-named public progress symbols. Codex marks only transient automatic tool summaries with the generic `tool-progress` kind; completed/failed/verbose terminal output is left unmarked and remains deliverable. target.title: fix(browser): run mutation guard before JSON parsing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser control mutation requests were parsed as JSON before the header-only mutation CSRF guard ran. A cross-site browser request with malformed JSON could therefore hit the JSON parser first and return a parser error instead of the stable `403 Forbidden` mutation-guard response.

## Why This Change Was Made

The mutation guard only needs request method and headers (`Origin`, `Referer`, and `Sec-Fetch-Site`). Running it before body parsing rejects unsafe browser-originated mutations earlier and avoids spending parser work on requests that should never reach route handling.

## User Impact

Cross-site mutation attempts against Browser control routes now fail closed before body parsing, even when their JSON payload is malformed or expensive to parse. Allowed local/CLI-style requests still pass through to the JSON parser and route handlers normally.

## Evidence

- Moved `browserMutationGuardMiddleware()` before `express.json()` in `extensions/browser/src/browser/server-middleware.ts`.
- Added focused middleware regressions in `extensions/browser/src/browser/server-middleware.test.ts` for:
  - cross-site malformed JSON returning `403 Forbidden` without invoking the route
  - allowed JSON requests still parsing and reaching the route
  - existing request signal behavior preserved

## Proof

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=.vitest-cache-browser-mutation-guard node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/server-middleware.test.ts`

target.title: feat(subagents): add execution backend placement contract
target.body:
## Summary

Adds the first real implementation slice for #82017: `sessions_spawn` now accepts an optional execution placement request and validates it against `agents.executionBackends`.

This PR keeps runtime behavior conservative: the built-in `local` `process` backend is the only executable backend in this release. Forward-looking `container` and `kubernetes` configs are accepted by config validation, but spawn rejects them with an explicit runtime-policy error until those backends are implemented. Placement is recorded on spawned run metadata/list output for readback; non-local runner dispatch is intentionally not implemented here.

## Related PRs

- Runtime self-context / runtime tool companion: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90101

## CONTRIBUTING alignment

- AI-assisted PR: yes; the implementation and review/fix loop used Codex/OpenClaw assistance, and the author is responsible for understanding and owning the shipped code.
- Current-head real behavior proof: included below for `ae6a3f7fdfb1`, covering default local process placement, configured local profile placement, and unsupported Kubernetes fail-closed behavior.
- Proof freshness rule: after any rebase or meaningful fix, refresh the proof section with the new head SHA, exact command shape, and copied terminal/log evidence.
- Bot review status: ClawSweeper has marked contributor proof sufficient and ready for maintainer look; the remaining action is maintainer approval of the public contract.
- Takeover readiness: maintainer edits are enabled, related PR #90101 is linked, and this PR intentionally does not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Maintainer contract decision requested

Please explicitly choose one before merge:

- Approve the v1 additive contract: `agents.executionBackends` plus `sessions_spawn.execution`, with only local `process` execution implemented in this slice and `container`/`kubernetes` configs accepted but rejected fail-closed at spawn time.
- Narrow before merge: restrict the schema/docs to local `process` only until non-local backend semantics are fully designed.
- Pause for broader design: hold this PR until runtime self-context, execution placement, and remote worker protocol decisions are reviewed together.

## Linked issue

Related to #82017.

## What changed

- Added `agents.executionBackends` config schema/types/help/labels/tags/docs.
- Added `sessions_spawn.execution.backend/profile` schema and plumbing.
- Added placement resolution for subagent and ACP spawns.
- Persisted execution placement into subagent run records and list output.
- Regenerated prompt snapshots for the new model-facing tool schema.
- Added unit coverage for config validation, placement resolution, tool parameter forwarding, and list readback.

## Behavior

- Omitted execution request defaults to `{ backend: "local", type: "process" }`.
- Configured local process profiles can be requested by name, validated, and recorded on the run.
- Unknown backends/profiles fail before spawn starts.
- `container`/`kubernetes` backends are schema-valid but rejected at spawn time for now.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: `sessions_spawn.execution` placement resolution accepts the default local process backend, accepts a configured local profile, and rejects an unsupported Kubernetes backend instead of silently falling back.
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw repository checkout at branch `feat/execution-backends-local`, rebased on `origin/main`, running the patched TypeScript source with Node/tsx.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```sh
node --import tsx <<'EOF'
import { resolveAgentExecutionPlacement } from './src/agents/execution-backends.ts';

const cfg = {
  agents: {
    executionBackends: {
      local: {
        type: 'process',
        profiles: {
          small: { resources: { requests: { cpu: '500m', memory: '1Gi' } } },
        },
      },
      k8s: {
        type: 'kubernetes',
        profiles: { 'large-build': {} },
      },
    },
  },
};

for (const [name, request] of [
  ['default local process', undefined],
  ['local small profile', { backend: 'local', profile: 'small' }],
  ['unsupported k8s backend', { backend: 'k8s', profile: 'large-build' }],
]) {
  console.log(`${name}: ${JSON.stringify(resolveAgentExecutionPlacement({ cfg, request }))}`);
}
EOF
```

- Evidence after fix (copied live terminal output):

```text
default local process: {"ok":true,"execution":{"backend":"local","type":"process"}}
local small profile: {"ok":true,"execution":{"backend":"local","type":"process","profile":"small"}}
unsupported k8s backend: {"ok":false,"error":"execution backend \"k8s\" has type \"kubernetes\", but only local process execution is supported in this release"}
```

- Observed result after fix: local process placement resolves successfully, the configured `small` profile is preserved in the placement result, and unsupported Kubernetes placement returns an explicit runtime-policy error.
- What was not tested: full non-local container/Kubernetes runner dispatch, because this PR intentionally does not implement non-local backend runners.

## Verification

Ran locally on branch `feat/execution-backends-local`:

- `pnpm tsgo:test:src`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/agents/execution-backends.ts src/agents/acp-spawn.ts src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-tool.ts src/agents/subagent-list.ts src/agents/subagent-list.test.ts src/config/zod-schema.agents.ts src/config/types.agents.ts src/config/schema.tags.ts src/config/schema.labels.ts`
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_INCLUDE_FILE=.vitest-include-help-quality node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.tooling.config.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.runtime-config.config.ts src/config/schema.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts src/agents/execution-backends.test.ts src/agents/subagent-list.test.ts`
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_INCLUDE_FILE=.vitest-include-agents node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts`
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_INCLUDE_FILE=.vitest-include-agents-tools node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-tools.config.ts`
- `pnpm config:docs:check`
- `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/gateway/config-agents.md docs/tools/subagents.md`
- `pnpm format:docs:check docs/gateway/config-agents.md docs/tools/subagents.md`
- `pnpm prompt:snapshots:check`
- `git diff --check`

## Security impact

No new secrets, network access, or remote execution implementation. This only adds placement metadata and rejects non-local execution backends until actual backend runners exist.

target.title: fix(agents): stuck recovery must not abort replacement embedded runs
target.body:
Closes #104589

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stuck-session recovery could abort or force-clear a **newer** embedded run that replaced an older generation under the same session ID. Operators saw redundant stuck-recovery cycles and healthy retries interrupted after a prior run failed to release cleanly.

## Why This Change Was Made

`abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` now captures the active handle at entry and binds abort, generation-aware drain wait, and optional force-clear to that generation. Administrative session-level and global abort APIs stay current-run cancellation paths. This matches ClawSweeper guidance to bind the full abort/wait/force-clear chain to one captured identity rather than only two guards.

## User Impact

Stuck recovery no longer cancels a healthy replacement run on the same session after a stale generation is selected. Normal user abort, restart, compaction, and session-reset cancellation behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.test.ts
# Test Files  1 passed (1)
# Tests  47 passed (47)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts \
  src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts
# Test Files  2 passed (2)
# Tests  31 passed (31)

pnpm check:changed -- \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-state.ts
# typecheck core/core tests: ok
# format: ok after oxfmt
# lint core changed files: ok after removing unnecessary String() casts

node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-state.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts
# Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
```

New focused cases:

- `does not abort or force-clear a replacement run after recovery captures the stale generation`
- `skips force-clear and generation wait when the captured handle was already replaced`

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: stuck recovery must not abort/force-clear a replacement embedded run under the same session ID after selecting a stale generation.
- Environment: local macOS (darwin), Node v24.17.0, openclaw checkout branch `fix/104589-embedded-run-identity` @ `145ae17b36eecc011dd4c4a1e76bfef9943f123b`.
- Current-main contrast: on main, `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` re-resolves the session ID for abort, session-only wait, and force-clear, so a mid-flight `setActiveEmbeddedRun` replacement can be aborted or deleted. `clearActiveEmbeddedRun` already used handle identity; abort/force-clear did not.
- **Runtime path exercised (not only unit assertions):** process-local registry + production `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession` → `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` with `reason=stuck_recovery`, `forceClear=true`, `allowActiveAbort=true`. During the captured generation's `abort()`, a replacement handle was registered under the same `sessionId`/`sessionKey` (the race operators hit).
- Exact command after this patch (local one-shot harness; no network/credentials):
  ```bash
  OPENCLAW_LOG_LEVEL=debug node --import tsx /tmp/openclaw-pr-104654-proof/replacement-survives-stuck-recovery.mts
  ```
- Evidence after fix (captured 2026-07-11 20:39 UTC):
  - stale generation aborted once (`staleAbortCount=1`)
  - replacement never aborted (`replacementAbortCount=0`)
  - replacement still active under the session key after recovery
  - recovery outcome: `status=aborted aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false released=0` in **41ms**
  - diagnostic log line: `stuck session recovery outcome: ... forceCleared=false`
- Terminal transcript (redacted: synthetic session ids only; no IPs/credentials/endpoints):

- Control check: sibling unit cases still pass (`force-clears an aborted run that does not drain`, pre-replaced generation skip). Prior stuck-recovery runtime/integration suites (31 tests) remained green on the PR head.
- Observed result after fix: production stuck-session recovery acts only on the captured generation; a newer run registered under the same session survives abort/drain of the stale generation with `forceCleared=false`.

target.title: feat: add runtime self context config and tool
target.body:
## Related issue

Implementation slice for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89537.

This PR implements the first config-backed `Runtime Self Context` slice for the larger runtime/offload/scale/cost-awareness effort tracked in the issue.

## Related PRs

- Runtime placement / execution backend companion: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84758

## CONTRIBUTING alignment

- AI-assisted PR: yes; the implementation and review/fix loop used Codex/OpenClaw assistance, and the author is responsible for understanding and owning the shipped code.
- Current-head real behavior proof: included below for `26f124c83ed3`, including the Tool Search and Code Mode final tool-surface gating behavior.
- Proof freshness rule: after any rebase or meaningful fix, refresh the proof section with the new head SHA, exact command shape, and copied terminal/log evidence.
- Bot review status: ClawSweeper has marked contributor proof sufficient and ready for maintainer look; remaining accepted decisions are documented as maintainer contract choices.
- Takeover readiness: maintainer edits are enabled, related PR #84758 is linked, and this PR intentionally does not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Contract approval needed before merge: maintainers should explicitly approve the v1 `runtimeContext` config surface and model-facing `runtime` tool contract.

## Goal

Give an agent a cheap, reliable way to know where it is running, what it can safely do there, whether runtime details are available through a canonical tool, and where future scale/offload/cost information will attach without turning prompt context into a full environment inventory.

Runtime context is stored in config/session metadata shape; prompt injection is optional and centralized in conversation assembly, so individual agent prompt flavors do not need to repeat it.

## Implemented v1 slice

- Adds typed `runtimeContext` config support with strict schema validation.
- Supports exposure modes: `none`, `tool_hint`, and `prompt_summary`.
- Injects runtime self-context through the existing hidden `openclaw.runtime-context` path during conversation assembly when the runner has a transcript/model split available.
- Keeps `none` fully silent: no prompt injection and no runtime tool.
- Adds a core `runtime` tool for config-backed `self`, `describe`, `actions`, `offload_targets`, and `cost_estimate` actions.
- Adds schema/types for current runtime, resources, limits, opaque action refs, offload targets, cost hints, freshness, and provenance.
- Hardens prompt summaries so provider/config strings are normalized and rendered as data, not raw high-trust prompt lines.
- Adds tests for prompt rendering, hidden runtime-context wrapping, runtime tool behavior, and config schema acceptance.
- Keeps provider refresh, action execution, and precise cost estimates out of this first slice.

## Team review findings addressed

- Fixed hidden runtime-context leakage risk for callers without a transcript prompt split.
- Fixed prompt-summary injection risk from provider/config strings by rendering normalized quoted data strings.
- Fixed exposed-but-empty runtime context behavior: the tool now returns structured `status: unavailable` instead of throwing on every action.
- Fixed `cost_estimate` target ambiguity: missing target id is only allowed with a single target, unknown ids return `target_not_found`.
- Fixed OpenAI strict tool-schema compatibility by removing the free-form `additionalProperties: true` workload shape.
- Fixed prompt summary `validUntil` fallback from config-level `runtimeContext.validUntil`.

target.body:
Related: #96625
Related: #88838

## What Problem This Solves

Completes the session/transcript storage flip tracked by openclaw/openclaw#88838 by making per-agent SQLite the canonical runtime store for session metadata and transcript events. Legacy `sessions.json` and active transcript JSONL files are now doctor import inputs or archive artifacts, not runtime fallback state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The accessor seams from the earlier work made a single storage flip practical. Shipping a mixed file/SQLite runtime would let session metadata and transcript rows drift, so this PR moves import, runtime access, retention, SDK cleanup, and ratchets together behind the permanent accessor boundary.

## User Impact

Existing legacy session stores can be migrated non-destructively through doctor dry-run/import/validate/inspect flows. Runtime session creation, resume, transcript append, compaction, and maintenance use SQLite rows; retention still exports archived JSONL artifacts before deleting rows so support and archive workflows keep inspectable artifacts.

target.title: feat(memory): add multi-slot memory role architecture
target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a memory-plugin architecture flaw: OpenClaw currently has one exclusive `plugins.slots.memory` owner even though the product, docs, bundled plugins, and runtime behavior already treat “memory” as several different responsibilities.

Today, factual recall, auto-capture, compaction, dreaming/consolidation, and user/session modeling are all forced through the same global selector. That makes documented memory stacks impossible or brittle: selecting one memory provider can unintentionally displace another provider that owns a different responsibility.

This PR corrects that mismatch by introducing purpose-specific memory role slots:

- `memory.recall`
- `memory.capture`
- `memory.compaction`
- `memory.dreaming`
- `memory.userModel`

The new role slots are the mechanism. The fix is that OpenClaw can now represent the memory architecture it already documents and partially implements.

## What Problem This Solves

This is a flaw fix, not just a feature request.

OpenClaw’s memory ecosystem is already multi-role:

- `memory-core` / QMD provide local factual recall/search over project memory, session transcripts, and Markdown/QMD corpora.
- Honcho provides cross-session user, agent, and session modeling.
- LanceDB provides embedding-backed long-term recall and auto-capture.
- Active Memory orchestrates recall before generation by using whichever provider owns recall.
- Memory Wiki compiles durable memory into a companion knowledge vault rather than replacing active memory.
- Dreaming/consolidation is a separate runtime responsibility from ordinary recall.

The current `plugins.slots.memory` contract cannot express that architecture. It treats every `kind: "memory"` provider as competing for one owner slot, even when the providers are designed to do different jobs. That leads to three concrete problems:

1. **Documented combinations are not representable.** Configs such as builtin/QMD recall + Honcho user modeling, LanceDB capture + local recall, or Active Memory over a selected recall provider cannot be modeled cleanly through one memory owner.
2. **Runtime behavior depends on exceptions and side paths.** Plugins that should compose have to rely on context-engine ownership, sidecar behavior, fallback logic, or plugin-specific handling instead of a shared contract.
3. **Diagnostics and lifecycle handling become misleading.** Startup, validation, status, doctor repair, skill publishing, uninstall cleanup, runtime memory resolution, and SDK-facing aliases need to know which provider owns which memory responsibility.

So while this PR adds new public config keys, the intent is corrective: make the config/runtime contract match the memory system OpenClaw already exposes.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

After this PR, OpenClaw can express memory stacks that were previously documented or implied but not cleanly configurable:

- `memory-core` or QMD can own factual recall while Honcho owns user/session modeling.
- LanceDB can own recall and/or capture without forcing unrelated memory roles through the same selector.
- Active Memory can use the configured `memory.recall` provider instead of depending on hard-coded assumptions.
- Dreaming/consolidation can be selected separately from ordinary recall where supported.
- Memory Wiki can remain a companion compiled-knowledge layer beside active memory providers.
- Existing configs using `plugins.slots.memory` continue to work as recall selection.
- `openclaw doctor --fix` can migrate/canonicalize non-conflicting legacy memory-slot config while preserving the legacy key for plugin compatibility.

## Linked Context

Closes #60572.

Directly related memory-composition requests and prior proposals:

- #38874: supplementary/additive memory plugins alongside the primary memory slot.
- #2306: earlier closed PR proposing stackable memory plugins.
- #2080: earlier request for multiple simultaneous memory plugins and emerging memory architectures.
- #77714: pluggable persistent memory backend demand.

Dreaming and memory-role separation context:

- #85473: future protocol work for making dreaming implementable by non-`memory-core` memory plugins. This PR adds the `memory.dreaming` slot contract but does not implement that full protocol.
- #63067 and #65411: prior work around keeping dreaming behavior available when another plugin owns the legacy memory slot.
- #62275: previous selected-slot dreaming config behavior.

Runtime/diagnostic slot handling context:

- #76567 and #76495: configured memory-slot runtime checks should load/consult the selected memory plugin.
- #78540: doctor/status memory diagnostics could misreport configured memory providers.
- #76550: stale `plugins.slots.*` references could leave config unrecoverable until doctor cleanup was broadened.

Context-engine compatibility context:

- #77063, #77185, #76576, and #81843: context-engine registration and LosslessClaw-adjacent failures shaped the compatibility review for preserving the existing global `plugins.slots.contextEngine` behavior while rejecting unsupported per-agent `contextEngine` config.

Future API/RFC context:

- #70823: future machine-readable slot ownership/provenance. This PR intentionally keeps scalar plugin IDs and solves the memory role composition layer first.

Memory-plugin interop research: the [supporting research document](https://github.com/kklouzal/rfcs/blob/rfc/multi-slot-memory-role-architecture/rfcs/0009/memory-plugin-interop-research.md) validates this PR as necessary architecture work, not optional extensibility: OpenClaw's own documentation already describes memory as a composable ecosystem where builtin/QMD recall, Honcho user/session modeling, LanceDB recall/capture, Active Memory orchestration, dreaming/consolidation, and Memory Wiki compilation can coexist, but current `origin/main` collapses every `kind: "memory"` provider into one exclusive `plugins.slots.memory` owner, making those documented combinations impossible or dependent on brittle exceptions. PR #88504 closes that product/docs/runtime gap by replacing the single memory owner with explicit role slots — `memory.recall`, `memory.capture`, `memory.compaction`, `memory.dreaming`, and `memory.userModel` — while preserving legacy `memory` as a recall shorthand, so the documented memory-plugin interop story becomes actually representable in config and runtime behavior.

## What Changes

- Adds canonical memory role slots: `memory.recall`, `memory.capture`, `memory.compaction`, `memory.dreaming`, and `memory.userModel`.
- Keeps legacy `plugins.slots.memory` as a backward-compatible shorthand for `memory.recall` during an extended migration window.
- Adds per-agent memory role-slot overrides under `agents.list[*].plugins.slots`, limited to memory roles plus legacy `memory`.
- Wires role-slot selection through config schema/types/help/docs, plugin activation, gateway startup preloading, runtime memory resolution, skill publishing, validation, doctor repair/preview, uninstall cleanup, status diagnostics, and SDK-facing aliases.
- Preserves the existing global `plugins.slots.contextEngine` path for LosslessClaw and other context-engine plugins.
- Explicitly rejects unsupported per-agent `agents.list[*].plugins.slots.contextEngine` overrides because agent-scoped context-engine semantics are outside this PR.

## Implementation Notes

- Adds `src/plugins/slot-resolution.ts` as the shared role-slot helper layer for canonical memory role keys, defaults, normalization, effective per-agent resolution, and configured selection collection.
- Updates config schema/types/help/labels/docs for global and per-agent memory role slots.
- Keeps `PluginSlotsConfig.contextEngine` for global plugin slots, and adds an agent-slot type/schema that omits `contextEngine`.
- Updates doctor legacy memory-slot handling so `doctor --fix` canonicalizes to `memory.recall` while retaining legacy `memory` during the compatibility window.
- Updates plugin loader/activation/startup resolution so explicit role-slot selections activate memory plugins without confusing default `memory-core` fallback with a user-selected plugin under restrictive allowlists.
- Extends validation to report missing role-slot plugin refs and validate schemas for plugins selected only by non-recall or per-agent memory roles.
- Extends skill publishing, status scanning, uninstall cleanup, memory runtime, dreaming, compaction provider, and SDK alias behavior to use the role-aware model.
- Keeps memory runtime registrations addressable by plugin id, so runtime recall dispatch follows the resolved global or per-agent `memory.recall` owner.
- Passes the session agent id into Pi embedded extension factory construction so safeguard compaction provider selection honors per-agent `memory.compaction` overrides in both normal session runs and manual/queued compaction paths.
- Updates bundled memory plugin manifests/docs to describe role support and the recall shorthand migration.

target.title: Fix compaction fallback for OpenAI Responses auth
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #98814.

OpenAI Responses auth already skips incompatible OAuth profiles while walking normal auth order, but compaction can pass the current session profile as an explicit `profileId`. For long direct sessions that inherited an OpenAI OAuth profile, this made `openai/openai-responses` throw before it could reach an API-key backup.

This PR now:

- adds an opt-in `fallbackOnIncompatibleProfile` resolver flag
- threads `authProfileIdSource` through embedded, manual/native, and harness compaction
- enables incompatible-profile fallback only for explicitly auto/inherited profiles
- keeps user-selected and missing/unknown-source profiles locked and fail-fast
- preserves profile source only while compaction stays on the same provider
- refreshes the branch onto upstream `main` at `262baedcf7fa`

Default explicit-profile behavior remains fail-fast outside this narrowly gated compaction path.

## What Problem This Solves

Long-running direct sessions can hit transcript compaction while using `openai/gpt-5.5` through an inherited OAuth profile. The compaction runtime then calls the OpenAI Responses API, which requires API-key auth. Auto/inherited profiles may now fall through to the configured API-key backup, while explicit user locks are never silently replaced.

## Evidence

Existing reporter proof is unchanged: live logs from a direct Signal session showed `compactionTokens=272001` followed by `Auth profile ... uses oauth auth, but openai/openai-responses requires an OpenAI API key profile.` After applying the local installed-dist patch through Hook 50 and restarting OpenClaw, `openclaw status` reported the gateway reachable and the session recovered to roughly `113k/272k` tokens.

## Regression Coverage Added

- resolver fallback from incompatible OAuth to API-key auth order
- default explicit-profile fail-fast behavior
- locked-profile fail-fast behavior even when fallback is requested
- auto vs. user vs. unknown compaction source policy
- source preservation on same-provider compaction and removal on provider switch
- direct compaction credential-lookup arguments for auto, user, and missing sources

## Validation

Historical validation performed before the original PR was opened:

target.title: fix: keep yielded parent runs deferred until subagents settle
target.body:
## Summary

This change promotes yielded-parent semantics into a shared parent lifecycle classifier and routes the affected cron, subagent-registry, and Discord/source-message paths through that state instead of letting each consumer infer completion from terminal-shaped model-attempt events, missing final text, or abort-shaped control flow.

The shipped behavior is:

- yielded parent + active descendants is treated as waiting/deferred, not ordinary completion;
- yielded parent + no descendant is treated as diagnostic error;
- cron delivery waits for a real final outcome instead of counting the yielded attempt as `ok / not-delivered`;
- Discord/source-message progress remains parent-owned while the yielded parent is waiting;
- descendant settlement wakes/reconciles yielded parents through the existing continuation paths.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where parent-agent runs that spawned child sessions/subagents and then called `sessions_yield` could look finished before the parent task actually completed.

The most visible failures were:

- isolated cron `agentTurn` jobs with valid delivery targets could finish as `ok / not-delivered` because the yielded parent had no final payload yet;
- Discord source-message lifecycle could clear parent progress/done indicators while child work was still active or while the parent was waiting to reconcile final output;
- run history/status surfaces made yielded parent work look like delivery failure, ordinary success with no output, or completed source-message work instead of a paused/resumable parent lifecycle.

`session_yield` is supposed to end the current model turn, not the parent task. This PR makes that distinction explicit for the affected runtime consumers.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

Operators and developers can now rely on `sessions_yield` after spawning child/subagent work without the parent run being misrepresented as complete at the cron or Discord lifecycle boundary.

Practically:

- autonomous development crons stop inflating misleading `ok / not-delivered` results for intentionally yielded runs;
- cron history exposes a distinct `deferred` state for yielded parent handoff;
- Discord progress no longer marks the parent source message done just because the parent yielded while children continue;
- yielded parent runs are resumed/reconciled when descendant work settles;
- debugging points to the parent/child lifecycle state instead of falsely implying delivery target resolution failed.

## Linked Context

- #95535 — `sessions_yield` isolated cron resumption/delivery gap.
- #92369 — subagent orchestration in isolated cron sessions needs reliable spawn/wait/aggregate semantics.
- #92116 — `sessions_yield` completion delivered as passive context can break orchestration loops.
- #86537 — subagent terminal reconciliation can expire suspended final delivery.
- #86538 — session write-lock timeouts can block subagent delivery lanes.
- #95833 — subagent abort-settle/session-lock failure can break session continuation.
- #92460 — isolated cron completion delivery gap around final controller return.
- #95604 — Discord subagent progress visibility.
- #94153 — durable queued subagent completion announcements.
- #95847 — requester-consumed descendant completion accounting.

## What Changes

### Shared parent lifecycle state

- Adds `src/agents/agent-lifecycle-parent-state.ts`.
- Classifies lifecycle events with explicit yielded/waiting vs terminal semantics.
- Exports the classifier through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime`.
- Routes subagent registry and Discord source-message handling through the classifier instead of local `yielded && paused` inference.

### Cron lifecycle and delivery

- Adds first-class cron run status `deferred`.
- Classifies yielded descendant handoff before delivery-mode branching, so text, structured payloads, `delivery.mode: none`, source-satisfied delivery, and normal direct delivery all share the same semantics.
- Prevents duplicate/interim parent announcements while descendants are active.
- Records yielded-without-descendant as explicit error diagnostic.
- Keeps deferred manual task runs active rather than failing them.
- Disables one-shot deferred cron jobs after handoff to avoid retry loops.

### Persistence, protocol, CLI, and UI

- Extends run-log JSON/SQLite encoding and status filtering for `deferred`.
- Extends Gateway protocol schemas and cron server filters.
- Extends CLI status/wait typing and docs.
- Extends hook-visible status typing.
- Adds Control UI status/filter labels and generated locale fallbacks.

### Parent/subagent reconciliation

- Tracks yielded/paused parents that still have pending descendants.
- Marks yielded parents with `wakeOnDescendantSettle` so they are resumed/reconciled when descendant work settles.
- Handles child success/failure settlement through existing subagent lifecycle recovery paths.
- Adds regression coverage for yielded parents being reconciled after child failure so diagnostics can wake the parent.

### Discord/source-message lifecycle

- Projects lifecycle events from agent execution into reply/channel handling.
- Uses the shared classifier to identify yielded/waiting parent state.
- Preserves in-progress/progress representation for yielded parents with active children.
- Avoids prematurely marking Discord status reactions done or clearing draft/progress state when the parent yielded and remains waiting.

### Concurrent user-message semantics

`docs/tools/subagents.md` documents the selected policy: if a human sends another message while a requester is yielded, the new message starts a normal turn for the same requester session. OpenClaw keeps the yielded run visible as waiting on descendant completion rather than converting it into a stale final reply; when descendant completion arrives, the completion event is handed back to the requester for synthesis.

target.body:
Closes #98287
Related: #98234 (non-duplicate reply-session initialization conflict/drop issue)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Signal users sending quoted replies could have the quoted target extracted into `ReplyToBody` metadata while the agent-facing `BodyForAgent` remained only the new ambiguous message, such as `Did this get done?`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal inbound handling now renders visible quoted-reply context directly into `BodyForAgent` as a clear blockquote while preserving clean `RawBody`, `CommandBody`, and `BodyForCommands` for command parsing and hooks. The shared inbound metadata renderer skips only the duplicate one-hop reply-target block when the Signal-generated wrapper exactly matches the expected quoted body and sender; richer `ReplyChain` context and ordinary user-authored blockquotes still render normally.

## User Impact

Signal quoted replies now carry the referenced message into agent-facing input, so agents can answer ambiguous followups using the intended quoted target. Plain non-quoted Signal messages remain unchanged, and quoted context is not duplicated in the model prompt when Signal has already inlined the generated quote block.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(exa): resolve search env secret refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/exa/src/exa-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` read Exa web-search credentials with `readConfiguredSecretString(...) ?? EXA_API_KEY`. That path accepts direct strings, but an env SecretRef in `tools.web.search.exa.apiKey` stays unresolved instead of reading the referenced environment variable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Exa should use the same provider-local credential resolver as the other web-search runtimes: direct config wins, configured env SecretRefs resolve before ambient env fallbacks, and unavailable SecretRefs fail closed instead of silently using `EXA_API_KEY`.

## User Impact

Users can configure Exa web search with an env SecretRef and get the referenced key at runtime without putting the raw key in config. If the referenced env var is missing, the tool reports the normal missing-key state instead of using an unrelated ambient Exa key.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/exa/src/exa-web-search-provider.test.ts`
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/exa/src/exa-web-search-provider.runtime.ts extensions/exa/src/exa-web-search-provider.test.ts`

- `git diff --check`

## Proof

The regression tests cover direct configured keys, `EXA_API_KEY` fallback with no configured key, configured env SecretRef precedence over `EXA_API_KEY`, and missing env/file SecretRefs returning no key without live credentials.

target.title: feat(discord): show subagent progress
target.body:
## Summary

Adds opt-in Discord-scoped sub-agent progress feedback on the original inbound Discord message, including count reactions, durable failure marker behavior, and typing keepalive while tracked work is active.

## What Problem This Solves

Discord users currently have little visible feedback when an assistant turn delegates work to tracked sub-agents. Long-running turns can look idle after the initial message even though background sub-agents are still running, and a sub-agent failure is not visible on the original Discord message.

Discord also cannot represent concurrent work by adding the same emoji reaction multiple times from the same bot/user, so progress needs a count-based reaction model instead of repeated identical reactions.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

Discord users get immediate, lightweight progress feedback during delegated work without waiting for the final assistant reply:

- `1️⃣`, `2️⃣`, etc. show the current active tracked sub-agent count for the turn
- the count reaction is replaced as the active count changes
- the count reaction disappears when no tracked sub-agents remain active
- `🔴` remains if any tracked sub-agent ends with a non-OK outcome
- typing stays active while tracked sub-agents are still running

Operators can configure the behavior with `channels.discord.subagentProgress`, including reaction progress, count emoji, failure emoji, typing keepalive, interval, and max-duration TTL.

The feature is best-effort and Discord-only. Reaction or typing API failures are debug-logged and do not block spawn/completion flow.

## Linked Context

No linked issues or external context were listed in the current PR body.

## What Changes

This PR adds Discord-scoped, best-effort sub-agent progress feedback on the original inbound Discord message. The feature is opt-in with `channels.discord.subagentProgress.enabled=true`.

When enabled:

- one configurable count reaction shows the number of currently active tracked sub-agents (`1️⃣` … `🔟` by default)
- count changes replace the previous count reaction instead of accumulating multiple ordinal reactions
- zero active tracked sub-agents removes the count reaction
- any non-OK completion leaves a durable configurable failure marker (`🔴` by default)
- Discord typing is kept alive independently while tracked sub-agents remain active, then stops when all tracked work finishes or the safety TTL expires

The implementation threads the source Discord message id through native `sessions_spawn`, tracked ACP spawn, requester origin metadata, and internal Discord progress hook handling so the Discord extension can target the correct parent message. Non-Discord callers and callers without a source message id keep existing behavior.

## Implementation Notes

- Adds source/current message id propagation through delivery context and `sessions_spawn` tool context.
- Carries that id into native sub-agent spawn and tracked ACP registration.
- Keeps public plugin hook/requester metadata narrow while the Discord extension uses an internal Discord-only event shape for source-message progress targeting.
- Emits progress cleanup at run completion even when ordinary `subagent_ended` delivery is deferred.
- Adds a Discord progress tracker keyed by account id, parent channel id, typing/thread target id, and source message id to avoid thread collisions.
- Tracks active run ids and derives the displayed count from current active set size.
- Replaces the displayed count reaction when the active count changes, removes it at zero, and caps counts above the configured emoji list to the final configured emoji.
- Uses `unref` on typing timers where supported so keepalive intervals do not keep Node alive.
- Updates Discord config schema, exported config types, UI hints, generated channel config metadata, and docs.

## Tests / Verification

Focused validation and static/config/docs gates are preserved under Evidence below.

## Evidence

### Rebase/Squash/Proof

- Common upstream base: `13ecca5408cbc94e66105608bfe770d0fc660d76` (`origin/main`, `fix(telegram): back off session init spool retries`)
- Previous PR head: `20a11bf331429ed2fd521636910b4aa07c5dcc24`
- Current PR head: `0f0ea76085d4ddc271aa25bab129f9c518f95992`
- Re-squashed to one commit on the common base; pushed with `--force-with-lease`.
- Removed invalid/unnecessary delivered-text visibility experiment from `d17f593b4d4428f6ba7318f55eb40d76c3932094`; legitimate Discord sub-agent progress behavior remains.

### ClawSweeper Requested Real Behavior Proof Coverage

ClawSweeper requested redacted live Discord proof for source-message progress behavior, not only tests. The requested coverage was: count reaction add/replace/remove behavior, normal channel context, thread/forum context, concurrent tracked sub-agents, typing keepalive while tracked work is active, typing stop/drain and TTL behavior, and durable failure-marker behavior after a true non-OK sub-agent lifecycle.

The live proof below covers those requested behaviors: normal channel success, thread-bound success, concurrent count replacement/increment/decrement/clear, typing keepalive/stop plus TTL guard logs, and a durable failure marker retained on the original source message after non-OK lifecycle. Private host/path/token/session/network values are redacted; Discord IDs/timestamps shown are included only where they are needed to tie the proof to the source-message behavior.

### Real / Live Behavior Proof

Live Discord API proof was run from the installed PR stack on Dev-01 using `OpenClaw 2026.6.10-beta.1` at local HEAD `f15c88bd6f9 stack: combine beta memory slots and Discord progress`, with:

- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.enabled=true`
- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.reactions.enabled=true`
- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.typing.enabled=true`

Observed live behavior in Discord:

- **Normal channel success:** a Discord-originated parent turn spawned a tracked sub-agent run (`8c6dbfa0-e021-4c3a-9992-328de22caa13`). The source Discord message showed the active count reaction while the child was running, typing stayed active during child work, and the count reaction was removed after the child completed. Child proof line: `NORMAL_SUCCESS_1_DONE 2026-06-22T04:48:33Z`.
- **Thread-bound success:** a thread-bound Discord sub-agent run (`01fa6443-4fc1-409d-9cf3-969ce433edbd`) completed successfully while progress was shown from the Discord parent context. Child proof line: `THREAD_SUCCESS_1_DONE 2026-06-22T04:49:50Z`.
- **Concurrent count replacement:** two overlapping tracked sub-agent runs (`4b2701ef-85b0-41d5-a87f-f72924e21869` and `9a5b1e70-5b3b-4820-bb5f-cb6cb7b2a926`) exercised count add/replace/remove behavior. The Discord source message count reaction incremented while both children were active, decremented as the first child completed, and cleared after the second child completed. Child proof lines: `CONCURRENT_SUCCESS_2_DONE 2026-06-22T05:06:23Z` and `CONCURRENT_SUCCESS_3_DONE 2026-06-22T05:06:36Z`.
- **Typing keepalive/stop:** Discord typing was visible while tracked sub-agents were active and stopped after tracked work drained. Earlier long-running proof passes also hit the configured typing safety TTL, with gateway logs showing `[typing] TTL exceeded (60000ms), auto-stopping typing indicator`, confirming the timeout guard executes.

Additional observation: after the final child drains, there can be a brief visual gap before the parent posts its final reconciliation response. That appears to be parent-yield lifecycle behavior rather than this PR's sub-agent progress tracker; it is being tracked separately as a follow-up investigation and is not treated as a blocker for this PR.

Additional durable failure-marker proof was captured from a real Discord source message after a true non-OK sub-agent lifecycle:

- **Failure marker:** source message `1518528276031602788` in Discord channel `1507934992699756645` retained the configured durable failure reaction `🔴` with count `1` and `me: true` after the non-OK sub-agent lifecycle. The source message timestamp was `2026-06-22T08:09:13.897Z`. A later follow-up heartbeat at `2026-06-22T08:29:48.355Z` reported a separate verification pass, confirming the red marker was left on the original source message rather than being ordinary final text delivery.

Redacted observation:

```json
{
  "channel_id": "1507934992699756645",
  "message_id": "1518528276031602788",
  "timestampUtc": "2026-06-22T08:09:13.897Z",
  "content": "Extensively check over the branch end-to-end against the recommended fix and prior investigation/research to ensure everything is clean, finalized, and polished.",
  "reactions": [
    {
      "emoji": { "name": "🔴" },
      "count": 1,
      "me": true
    }
  ]
}
```

## Compatibility and Risk

The feature is best-effort and Discord-only. Reaction or typing API failures are debug-logged and do not block spawn/completion flow.

Tests: 11 files, +1232 / -20
Total: 40 files, +2078 / -101

## Reviewer Checklist

- Confirm Discord progress remains opt-in and best-effort.
- Review source-message id propagation and tracker keying for channel/thread isolation.
- Confirm live Discord proof and focused tests cover add/replace/remove reactions, failure marker, typing, and config behavior.

---
Maintenance update: squashed to `381aa6f701d588adc4f18fd9dffcb84d6b41b953` after test-surface optimization only; behavior coverage and focused validation were preserved.

target.title: refactor(config): retire legacy flat streaming keys to doctor-owned migration [HOLD: compat decision]
target.body:
Related: #104318

## ⚠️ HOLD — maintainer decision required before merge

This PR is compatibility-sensitive and should NOT be merged without an explicit call on two points:
1. **Existing flat-key configs become hard-invalid at startup** (config validation fails, non-allowlisted commands exit 1, gateway startup-checkpoint refuses ready) until the user runs `openclaw doctor --fix`. Doctor config-rule fixes are NOT auto-applied on startup (verified: `runDoctorConfigPreflight` migrates state + relocates the config file only, not key shapes). Settings do not silently revert — the existing "Legacy config keys detected → Fix: openclaw doctor --fix" machinery names the exact keys — but a currently-working config becomes a startup failure until the operator acts.
2. **Timing vs the deprecation record**: `doctor-channel-streaming-aliases` records `removeAfter 2026-07-26`; this removes the runtime tolerance ~15 days early (2026-07-11). The doctor `--fix` migration is retained past that date.

## What Problem This Solves

Six legacy flat streaming keys (streamMode, chunkMode, blockStreaming, draftChunk, blockStreamingCoalesce, nativeStreaming) were normalized at steady-state load time, keeping non-canonical shapes alive in the runtime path against the repo's doctor-first rule (runtime reads canonical config only; older shapes migrate in doctor).

## Why This Change Was Made

Load-time normalization for these keys is removed so runtime consumes only the nested `streaming.*` shape; `openclaw doctor --fix` migrates flat→nested for every channel that supports them. Filled coverage gaps: discord had a migration but no rules (added 2); imessage/msteams had neither (added rules+migrations). Fixed two shared-migration bugs found en route: flat keys weren't removed when the nested key was already set, and a streamMode-conflict removal produced empty changes that doctor discarded (leaving config invalid after --fix). Five channels keep flat keys canonical for now (signal, irc, googlechat, whatsapp, mattermost + the SDK reply-runtime shape) — documented follow-up territory, not silently dropped.

## User Impact

See HOLD section. For migrated-config users: none. For flat-key users: a one-time `doctor --fix` requirement, loudly signposted.

## Evidence

- Testbox `tbx_01kx9c9532h5mesb0cej7h5w8c`: full battery + `pnpm check:changed`, exit 0; repo-wide `oxfmt --check` green up front; all tsgo lanes green.
- Doctor migration idempotence + per-key mapping tests; runtime-rejects-flat-keys tests.
- Autoreview (codex gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh), 3 rounds: two accepted fixes (SDK test flat-fallback assertions; streamMode silent-removal); one rejected with an inline invariant (no channel policy in core). Final clean (0.93).

target.title: fix(subagents): credit requester-consumed descendant completions
target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a lifecycle/delivery accounting gap for background and cron-owned subagent trees: when a requester actually consumes completed descendant subagent output, the descendant run is now durably credited as delivered instead of later being finalized as failed/suspended solely because no separate visible delivery event occurred.

## What Problem This Solves

Requester-owned subagent trees can legitimately consume descendant output without sending a separate descendant-visible delivery event. This is common for cron/background flows where a parent/requester gathers frozen child output, composes its own result, and then delivers that requester result outward. Before this PR, the descendant completion could remain delivery-unproven even though its output had already been consumed by the requester. Later cleanup/finalization could then classify that descendant as failed or suspended, producing delivery state that did not match real behavior. This PR gives the registry an explicit durable signal for that case: requester consumption is delivery evidence only for the exact descendant runs that were consumed, under the matching requester session/run-start window, when the requester path adopts descendant fallback output, so the consumed descendant rows do not later announce or finalize as pending just because the final outward send fails.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

When OpenClaw can prove that a requester consumed descendant subagent output, the matching descendant run receives durable delivery credit:
- `delivery.status` is set to `"delivered"` for the matched descendant completion;
- requester-consumption metadata is persisted with the run/delivery state;
- cleanup/finalize treats `delivery.status === "delivered"` as completed delivery proof;
- normal visible-delivery paths remain required for completions that were not consumed by a requester.
The matching is intentionally narrow. Credit is only applied when all of these are true:
- the consumed run IDs are explicit;
- the requester session key matches;
- the requester run-start window matches the consuming requester run;
- the consumption kind is known;
- cron fallback credit happens when cron adopts explicit descendant fallback output for the requester result;
- nested subagent announcement credit only covers direct child run IDs that were actually included in the requester-consumed output.

This PR keeps the delivery model explicit:
- if a descendant result was visibly delivered, it is delivered;
- if a requester consumed the descendant output because cron adopted it as the requester result, the descendant is delivered by requester consumption;
- if neither happened, failure/suspension handling still applies.

## Linked Context

- Related issue: #92433 — subagent completion can be silently dropped when an announce handoff reaches a requester transcript but the requester run ends before consuming it. This PR addresses the adjacent durable-accounting problem for completions that *are* consumed by a requester.
- Related issue: #67777 — subagent completion delivery can be lost on direct-announce timeout, drain, or orphan prune. This PR does not implement the full durable inbox/spool requested there, but it narrows one delivery-accounting gap by recording proven requester consumption.
- Related issue: #86537 — suspended final delivery can expire and discard a pending subagent completion. This PR keeps requester-consumed completions from remaining indistinguishable from undelivered completions in finalization state.
- Related issue: #90299 — subagent lifecycle state can report lost active execution context while still surfacing child output. This PR contributes to lifecycle/state consistency when descendant output is actually consumed.
- Related PR: #92934 — required assistant acknowledgement for completion wake handoffs, so transcript commit alone is not treated as requester consumption. This PR complements that by adding durable credit for explicit consumed descendant run IDs.
- Related PR: #35080 — deterministic subagent announce delivery with descendant gating. This PR builds on that direction by making consumed descendant accounting durable.
- Related PR: #44205 — stale descendant cron fallback summaries. This PR keeps the same stale-vs-current discipline for requester-consumed descendant credit.
- Related PR: #95604 — Discord subagent progress feedback. This PR is not a Discord UI change, but accurate delivered/failed lifecycle state is useful to progress/failure-marker consumers.
No exact existing issue/PR was found for `markDescendantCompletionConsumedByRequester` or this exact requester-consumed credit mechanism, so this PR should stand as the focused implementation thread for that behavior.

## What Changes

When OpenClaw can prove that a requester consumed descendant subagent output, the matching descendant run receives durable delivery credit:
- `delivery.status` is set to `"delivered"` for the matched descendant completion;
- requester-consumption metadata is persisted with the run/delivery state;
- cleanup/finalize treats `delivery.status === "delivered"` as completed delivery proof;
- normal visible-delivery paths remain required for completions that were not consumed by a requester.
The matching is intentionally narrow. Credit is only applied when all of these are true:
- the consumed run IDs are explicit;
- the requester session key matches;
- the requester run-start window matches the consuming requester run;
- the consumption kind is known;
- cron fallback credit happens when cron adopts explicit descendant fallback output for the requester result;
- nested subagent announcement credit only covers direct child run IDs that were actually included in the requester-consumed output.

## Implementation Notes

Core registry/runtime changes:
- Adds requester-consumed delivery metadata to subagent registry/delivery state.
- Adds a registry operation for marking descendant completions consumed by requester.
- Persists/restores the new delivery fields.
- Exposes the new runtime operation through the existing registry runtime shims.
Main files:
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-consumption.ts`
  - Implements durable requester-consumption credit.
  - Matches by requester session, explicit run IDs, and run-start window.
  - Records requester-consumption metadata and persists the updated run state.
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.types.ts`
  - Adds delivery/requester-consumption state fields.
- `src/agents/subagent-delivery-state.ts`
  - Persists and restores the new delivery fields.
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-runtime.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.registry.runtime.ts`
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-subagent-registry.runtime.ts`
  - Wires the new registry operation through runtime boundaries.
Requester-consumption paths:
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/subagent-followup.ts`
  - Reads completed descendant fallback replies and returns both formatted fallback text and the consumed descendant run IDs.
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.ts`
  - Applies cron fallback consumption credit when cron adopts explicit descendant fallback output, before the final outbound send.
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`
  - Credits nested/direct child completions when their output is included in the requester-consumed announcement/wake result.
  - Uses the same latest-child dedupe input for rendering and consumed-run credit so stale child rows are not credited.
- `src/agents/subagent-announce-output.ts`
  - Keeps latest-child dedupe reusable while preserving caller-specific fields such as `runId`.

## Tests / Verification

Coverage added or extended for:
- positive requester-consumed descendant credit;
- no credit for mismatched requester session;
- no credit outside the requester run-start window;
- no credit without explicit consumed run IDs;
- persisted/restored requester-consumption delivery fields;
- cron fallback credit only after successful outbound delivery;
- cleanup/finalize treating `delivery.status === "delivered"` as proof;
- nested/direct child announcement credit;
- stale-vs-current child dedupe, including a negative assertion that stale child run IDs are not credited when stale output is not rendered.
Primary test files:
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-consumption.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-delivery-state.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-completion.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.lifecycle-retry-grace.e2e.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.format.e2e.test.ts`
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/subagent-followup.test.ts`
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.double-announce.test.ts`

## Evidence

### Rebase/Squash/Proof

- Common upstream base: `13ecca5408cbc94e66105608bfe770d0fc660d76` (`origin/main`, `fix(telegram): back off session init spool retries`)

SQLite persistence now derives `pending_final_delivery` only from active delivery statuses (`pending`, `in_progress`, `suspended`), so delivered/requester-consumed rows that retain payload metadata do not rehydrate as pending.

target.title: Fix stack-safe large attachment handling
target.body:
## Summary

Closes #90098.

This branch is now rebased onto current OpenClaw architecture and deliberately narrowed to the parts still missing from `main`:

- replace the gateway's full-payload data-URL capture regex with bounded index/slice parsing;
- replace the Control UI send-path data-URL capture regex in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.ts`;
- replace the pasted-image full-payload regex in `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-composer.ts` with a bounded header check plus iterative payload validation;
- discard stale failed composer queue entries created by the old `Maximum call stack size exceeded` failure;
- add focused gateway and current-UI regression coverage.

Current `main` already contains iterative base64 validation and the broader 20 MB / 20-page inbound extraction policy, so this update keeps those upstream implementations and drops the obsolete extraction-limit/config churn from the older branch.

## What problem this solves

Multi-megabyte PDF/image data URLs were still passed through regexes that captured the entire base64 payload. On sufficiently large browser or gateway sends, V8 could throw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` before the attachment reached normal validation/offload handling. Failed Control UI sends carrying that historical error could also be restored and replayed after upgrade.

The new parsing keeps regex use bounded to a short MIME header and processes the payload by index/iteration.

## Current changed paths

- `src/gateway/chat-attachments.ts`
- `src/gateway/chat-attachments.test.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-composer.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/composer-persistence.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/composer-persistence.test.ts`

## Verification

Regression coverage on the current file layout now includes:

- a 12 MiB gateway data URL parsed/offloaded without a full-payload regex;
- a large Control UI attachment serialized through `chat.send`;
- a large pasted image converted through the current composer;
- rejection of invalid pasted base64;
- identifiable pre-fix attachment stack-overflow records dropped during restore, while current failures and unrelated text failures with the same generic V8 phrase remain durable and retryable via a stored item-format marker.

Fresh GitHub CI is running on exact head `73169d41851fa41bbe502df3cab0e04d3f448a7c`, which contains the shared upstream cutoff `262baedcf7fa3d66dc35cce7d0253e0a31f0cc0e` and the narrowed legacy-cleanup repair.

Additional exact-head repair validation: 281 focused Control UI tests pass across composer persistence, chat state, and chat send; formatting, targeted oxlint, and diff checks also pass. The storage-only marker is retained across internal normalization only for affected failed attachment records and is stripped from public queue snapshots.

## Real behavior evidence

The original branch was validated with a real Chrome upload of a 9.18 MB, 8-page PDF (roughly a 12 MB base64 data URL) against a live gateway. The upload completed without `RangeError`, was offloaded, and the model received extracted page content. That live run was on the pre-port head; this update ports the same stack-safe parsing behavior to today's gateway and UI paths and adds exact-path regression tests. No new live Signal/provider/device claim is being made for this merge-only port.

Generated with AI assistance; all security-sensitive parsing remains fail-closed for malformed payloads.

target.title: fix(gemini): resolve search env secret refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gemini web_search runtime credential resolution treated configured SecretRefs differently from direct string keys. A configured `plugins.entries.google.config.webSearch.apiKey` env SecretRef could be skipped at runtime, allowing the ambient `GEMINI_API_KEY` fallback or the Google model-provider key to be used instead.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gemini runtime already supports direct plugin search keys, ambient `GEMINI_API_KEY`, and model-provider key fallback. It should also honor the same SecretRef credential contract used by other web_search providers: configured env SecretRefs resolve to their referenced env value, and configured-but-unavailable SecretRefs fail closed instead of silently switching accounts.

## User Impact

Users who store the Gemini search API key as an env SecretRef now get the intended credential at request time. If that referenced secret is missing, Gemini web_search returns the existing missing-key diagnostic before any fetch is attempted instead of using another fallback key.

## Evidence

- Updated Gemini runtime credential resolution in `extensions/google/src/gemini-web-search-provider.runtime.ts`.
- Added focused regressions in `extensions/google/web-search-provider.test.ts` for:
  - configured Gemini env SecretRefs beating `GEMINI_API_KEY`
  - unavailable configured SecretRefs not falling back to env/provider credentials
  - Google model-provider env SecretRefs still working as fallback when no Gemini search key is configured

## Proof
